mainTopic: The גר תושב and גלות, and whether one who thought killing was permitted (אומר מותר) is close to מזיד or אנוס
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier answer: a blow that caused less than a פרוטה of damage brings מלקות, since there is no money to pay. On this view we do not compare hitting to cursing. Next the גמרא asks about the גר תושב in the משנה. רב כהנא explains that he goes to גלות for killing another גר תושב, but not for killing a Jew. The same split settles two פסוקים about the ערי מקלט. A ברייתא then seems to say a גר תושב is always executed, like a non-Jew. רב חסדא answers by contrasting a downward motion with an upward one, but רבא rejects this with a קל וחומר. רבא instead says the ברייתא is about אומר מותר, which he treats as close to מזיד, while רב חסדא calls it אנוס. Each side then brings proofs from the story of אבימלך and שרה, and the answer to אביי's challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A blow worth less than a פרוטה brings מלקות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier answer. The case of getting lashes for hitting is a blow that caused less than a פרוטה of damage, and it brings a source from רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is a blow that did not cause even a פרוטה worth of damage. As רבי אמי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone hit another person with a blow worth less than a פרוטה, he gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from before: it explains which kind of hitting brings מלקות. It is a blow that caused less than a פרוטה of damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person who hits someone pays money instead of getting lashes. When the damage is less than a פרוטה there is nothing to pay, so the Torah's prohibition is punished with מלקות instead. רבי יוחנן's statement is brought as the source for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount of money that counts in halacha
A blow; hitting someone
He gets lashes (מלקות)

steps.confusionAlert: The section opens in the middle of a sentence. The words שאין בה שוה פרוטה finish an answer that started on the previous page.

phrases.english: that does not have the value of a peruta.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page. It's about a blow that did less than a פרוטה of damage.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If he struck him a blow
that does not have the value of a peruta, he is flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun before this section
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hitting someone only leads to paying money, so it could never bring מלקות
steps.terutzMaskana: When the blow is worth less than a פרוטה, there is no payment, so the hitter gets מלקות

steps.title: Hitting is not compared to cursing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out what follows from this answer: we do not treat the laws of hitting the same as the laws of cursing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not compare hitting to cursing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a side lesson from the answer it just gave: hitting and cursing are not judged by the same rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some opinions learn the laws of hitting from the laws of cursing. This answer only works if we do not compare the two. So the rules that limit when cursing is punished do not automatically apply to hitting.

keyTerms.meaning: We compare; we learn one law from another
Cursing

steps.whatToRemember: A blow worth less than a פרוטה brings מלקות, and on this view hitting is judged by its own rules, not by the rules of cursing.

phrases.english: And we do not compare striking to cursing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from the answer in step 1
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: On this approach, the laws of hitting are not learned from the laws of cursing

steps.title: The משנה seems to treat a גר תושב like a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exception for a גר תושב and infers that a גר תושב has the status of a non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: everyone is sent to גלות for killing a Jew, except a גר תושב. This shows that a גר תושב is treated like a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It quotes the משנה about a גר תושב and draws an inference from it, which sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a גר תושב is not sent to גלות when he kills a Jew. From this the גמרא infers that a גר תושב is treated like a non-Jew, since non-Jews do not get the atonement of גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew who accepted the seven Noahide laws and lives in the Land of Israel
So it seems; this shows that
A non-Jew

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מֵעַל יְדֵי גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Except for due to a ger toshav, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: everyone is sent to גלות for killing a Jew, except a גר תושב.

phrases.english: Apparently, a ger toshav is a gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the רישא of the משנה, a גר תושב appears to have the status of a non-Jew

steps.title: The סיפא says a גר תושב goes to גלות
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא of the משנה says a גר תושב is sent to גלות for killing another גר תושב. That treats him unlike a non-Jew, so it seems to contradict the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the end of the משנה: a גר תושב is sent to גלות for killing a גר תושב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own inference using the end of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Non-Jews are never sent to גלות. If a גר תושב goes to גלות for killing another גר תושב, he is not being treated like a non-Jew. So the רישא and the סיפא seem to disagree about his status.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a משנה
Is sent to גלות in a city of refuge

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב גּוֹלֶה עַל יְדֵי גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב!
phrases.english: A ger toshav is exiled due to a ger toshav!

steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a גר תושב is a non-Jew
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A non-Jew never goes to גלות, yet the סיפא sends a גר תושב to גלות

steps.title: It depends on whom he killed
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the two parts of the משנה deal with different victims. A גר תושב who killed a גר תושב goes to גלות. A גר תושב who killed a Jew does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: there is no difficulty. Here the case is a גר תושב who killed a גר תושב. There the case is a גר תושב who killed a Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא settles the contradiction by showing that each part of the משנה is talking about a different victim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא, where he goes to גלות, is about killing another גר תושב. The רישא, where he does not go, is about killing a Jew. So גלות works for a גר תושב only when he kills someone of his own kind.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... there; each source deals with a different case

steps.whatToRemember: A גר תושב goes to גלות for killing a גר תושב, but not for killing a Jew.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: It is not difficult.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בְּגֵר תּוֹשָׁב שֶׁהָרַג גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב,
phrases.english: Here, it is about a ger toshav who killed a ger toshav;
phrases.notes: "Here" is the סיפא, where he goes to גלות.

phrases.english: there, it is about a ger toshav who killed a Jew.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא and the סיפא disagree about whether a גר תושב is like a non-Jew
steps.terutzMaskana: The victim decides the outcome: killing a גר תושב leads to גלות, killing a Jew does not

steps.title: Two פסוקים about ערי מקלט seem to disagree
steps.stepSummary: Some raise a contradiction between two פסוקים. One says the ערי מקלט are also for the גר תושב. The other says "for you", which implies they are not for גרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some point out two פסוקים that seem to clash. One says: "For the children of Israel, and for the stranger and the resident among them, these six cities shall be." Another says: "The cities shall be for you for refuge", meaning for you and not for גרים!
steps.whatsHappening: The same question now comes up from the פסוקים themselves: one פסוק includes the גר תושב in the ערי מקלט, and the other seems to leave him out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: במדבר 35:15 clearly lists the תושב as someone the cities protect. במדבר 35:12 says "for you", and the word "you" seems to mean only Jews. Read this way, the second פסוק excludes the גר תושב.

keyTerms.meaning: Points out that two פסוקים seem to contradict each other
Refuge; the ערי מקלט for someone who killed by accident

phrases.english: There are those who raise a contradiction between verses.
It is written: "For the children of Israel and for the stranger and for the resident among them
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:15

phrases.english: shall these six cities be."
And it is written: "And the cities shall be for you for refuge."
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:12

phrases.english: "For you", and not for strangers!
phrases.notes: "Strangers" here means people who are a גר תושב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the same question from the פסוקים instead of from the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים about who may use the ערי מקלט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק includes the גר תושב, while the other seems to exclude him with the word "for you"

steps.title: The same split settles the פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא gives the same answer. The פסוק that excludes him is about a גר תושב who killed a Jew. The פסוק that includes him is about a גר תושב who killed a גר תושב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: there is no difficulty. Here the case is a גר תושב who killed a Jew. There the case is a גר תושב who killed a גר תושב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא solves the clash between the פסוקים with the same split he used for the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "For you and not for גרים" refers to a גר תושב who killed a Jew, so he gets no refuge. The פסוק that includes the תושב refers to one who killed another גר תושב. The order of the cases is reversed here, but the rule is the same as in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jew

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: It is not difficult.
Here, it is about a ger toshav who killed a Jew;
phrases.notes: "Here" is the "for you and not for גרים" פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן – בְּגֵר תּוֹשָׁב שֶׁהָרַג גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב.
phrases.english: there, it is about a ger toshav who killed a ger toshav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 6
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים disagree about whether a גר תושב can use the ערי מקלט
steps.terutzMaskana: A גר תושב who killed a גר תושב uses the ערי מקלט; one who killed a Jew does not

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say a גר תושב is always put to death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists a גר תושב together with a non-Jew as people who are executed for killing. A non-Jew is executed no matter whom he killed, so the same should be true of a גר תושב. That leaves no room for גלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now a contradiction from a ברייתא: "Therefore a גר and a non-Jew who killed are executed." The ברייתא puts the גר next to the non-Jew. A non-Jew is executed whether he killed one of his own kind or someone else. So a גר should also be executed whether he killed one of his own kind or someone else!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא's answer with a ברייתא. Because the ברייתא lists the גר together with the non-Jew, the גר seems to be executed even for killing another גר תושב, so he would never go to גלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-Jew who kills, even by accident, is executed, whether the victim was a non-Jew or a Jew. Since the ברייתא lists the גר with the non-Jew, the גמרא reads them as having the same rule. That clashes with רב כהנא, who said a גר תושב who killed a גר תושב goes to גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction (from another source)
Similar to; listed in the same way
It makes no difference
One of his own kind
Is executed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא says outright that a גר who killed a גר is executed. The גמרא learns this only from the fact that the גר and the non-Jew are listed together.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
Therefore, a ger and a gentile who killed are executed.
phrases.notes: The "גר" here is a גר תושב.

phrases.english: It teaches the ger like the gentile:

phrases.aramaic: מָה גּוֹי לָא שְׁנָא דִּקְטַל בַּר מִינֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: Just as for a gentile, it makes no difference whether he killed one of his kind,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא דִּקְטַל דְּלָאו בַּר מִינֵיהּ – נֶהֱרָג,
phrases.english: or whether he killed one not of his kind, he is executed,
phrases.notes: "One not of his kind" means a Jew.

phrases.aramaic: אַף גֵּר, לָא שְׁנָא דִּקְטַל בַּר מִינֵּיהּ
phrases.english: so too a ger: it makes no difference whether he killed one of his kind

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא קְטַל דְּלָאו בַּר מִינֵיהּ – נֶהֱרָג!
phrases.english: or whether he killed one not of his kind, he is executed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי לְפִיכָךְ גֵּר וְגוֹי שֶׁהָרְגוּ נֶהֱרָגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's split from steps 5 and 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's rule that a גר תושב who killed a גר תושב goes to גלות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists the גר like a non-Jew, who is executed no matter whom he killed, so the גר should also be executed even for killing a גר תושב
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next stage of the סוגיא, where the גמרא will need to explain how the ברייתא fits with the משנה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: downward motion versus upward motion
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the משנה (גלות) is about a killing in a downward motion, and the ברייתא (death) is about a killing in an upward motion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is not difficult. Here, he killed him in a downward motion. There, he killed him in an upward motion. In a downward motion, where a Jew would go to גלות, exile is enough for the גר תושב too. In an upward motion, where a Jew would be exempt, the גר תושב is executed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the contradiction from step 8 by splitting the cases by how the accidental killing happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a Jew, a killing in a downward motion brings גלות, while an upward motion is exempt from גלות. רב חסדא says a גר תושב matches a Jew in the downward case and goes to גלות, as the משנה says. In the upward case there is no גלות for him, so he falls back to death, as the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: In a downward motion; a Jew who kills this way by accident goes to גלות
In an upward motion; a Jew who kills this way by accident is exempt from גלות
It is enough for him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the upward case is worse for a Jew. For a Jew it is lighter, since he is exempt from גלות. Only for the גר תושב does רב חסדא make it lead to death, and that is exactly what רבא attacks next.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is not difficult.
Here, it is where he killed him in a downward motion,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the משנה, which sends him to גלות. "There" is the ברייתא, which says he is executed.

phrases.english: there, it is where he killed him in an upward motion.
In a downward motion, where a Jew goes to exile,
for him too, exile is enough.
In an upward motion, where a Jew is exempt,
phrases.notes: Exempt from גלות. This follows the earlier משנה in this פרק about downward and upward motion.

phrases.english: he is executed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different ways of killing (downward versus upward).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא give two different punishments for the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a downward-motion killing, which brings גלות. The ברייתא is about an upward-motion killing, which brings death for a גר תושב.

steps.title: רבא: the reasoning should run the other way
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב חסדא with a קל וחומר. If the more serious downward case only brings גלות, the lighter upward case cannot bring death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Isn't it a קל וחומר the other way? If in a downward motion, where a Jew goes to גלות, exile is enough for the גר תושב, then in an upward motion, where a Jew is exempt, should the גר תושב be executed?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב חסדא's answer and shows that it turns the punishments upside down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upward case is the lighter one, since even a Jew gets no גלות for it. It makes no sense for the lighter case to bring a heavier punishment (death) than the serious case (only גלות). If anything, the upward case should be lighter for the גר תושב too.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one (or the reverse)
And is it not...? A rhetorical question that opens a challenge
And if...; the usual opening of a קל וחומר
Exempt

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But isn't it a קל וחומר?
phrases.notes: He means the קל וחומר points the opposite way from רב חסדא's answer.

phrases.english: If in a downward motion, where a Jew goes to exile,
for him too exile is enough,
then in an upward motion, where a Jew is exempt,
should he be executed?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חסדא's answer from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the upward-motion killing brings death for a גר תושב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: the lighter case (upward) cannot bring a harsher punishment than the more serious case (downward).

steps.title: רבא's own answer: he thought it was allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא, which says he is executed, is about a גר תושב who killed because he thought it was permitted (אומר מותר).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The ברייתא is about one who says it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב חסדא, רבא gives a new way to split the משנה from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (גלות) is about a plain accident. The ברייתא (death) is about a גר תושב who meant to kill but thought the killing was allowed. So the split is about the killer's state of mind, not the direction of his motion.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier answer and brings a new one
One who says it is permitted; he killed on purpose but wrongly thought it was allowed
Permitted

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is about one who says it is permitted.
phrases.notes: This explains the ברייתא, where he is executed. A plain accident still brings גלות, as the משנה says.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חסדא's answer, which was rejected in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different state of mind of the killer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between the משנה and the ברייתא is the direction of the motion.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about אומר מותר, who is executed. The משנה is about a plain accident, which brings גלות.

steps.title: אביי: someone who thought it was allowed is not at fault
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that one who thought the killing was allowed is an אנוס, so how can he be executed?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: One who says it is permitted is an אנוס!
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the killer truly did not know the killing was forbidden, he acted out of ignorance he could not help. That should make him less guilty, not deserving of death.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who acted under circumstances beyond his control, so he is not held at fault

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
One who says it is permitted is forced by circumstances!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אוֹמֵר מוּתָּר אָנוּס הוּא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that אומר מותר is executed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One who did not know the act was forbidden is an אנוס and should not get the harshest punishment.

steps.title: רבא: thinking it is allowed is close to doing it on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that אומר מותר is not treated as an אנוס. Since he meant to kill, it is close to מזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For I say that one who says it is permitted is close to intentional.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his answer against אביי's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא looks at the act itself. The killer chose to kill this person on purpose. His wrong idea that it was allowed does not turn him into an innocent victim of circumstance. So he is judged almost like a deliberate killer, and death makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to intentional
One who sins on purpose
For I say; introduces the speaker's own reasoning

phrases.english: He said to him: For I say,
one who says it is permitted is close to intentional.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר, אוֹמֵר מוּתָּר קָרוֹב לְמֵזִיד הוּא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the category: אומר מותר is close to מזיד, not אונס.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One who thought the killing was allowed is an אנוס.
steps.terutzMaskana: One who thought the killing was allowed is close to מזיד, so the ברייתא can rule that he is executed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final answer: the משנה (גלות) is a plain accident, while the ברייתא (death) is אומר מותר, which רבא treats as close to מזיד.

steps.title: רבא and רב חסדא follow their usual views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבא and רב חסדא disagree about אומר מותר in another case too. One who thought he was killing an animal or a non-Jew is liable according to רבא and exempt according to רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they follow their own reasoning, as it was stated: If he thought it was an animal and it turned out to be a person, or a non-Jew and it turned out to be a גר תושב, רבא says he is liable, since one who says it is permitted is close to intentional. רב חסדא says he is exempt, since one who says it is permitted is an אנוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the argument here matches a known dispute between רבא and רב חסדא in a similar case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both places the question is the same: is someone who thought the killing was allowed close to מזיד or an אנוס? רבא says close to מזיד, so he is liable. רב חסדא says אנוס, so he is exempt. That explains why רב חסדא did not use רבא's answer here.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning; each sage stays consistent with a view he holds elsewhere
As if he thought
And it turned out to be
Liable (here, to be executed)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the two answers in this סוגיא come from a deeper disagreement about how to judge a killer who thought the act was allowed.

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning,
phrases.notes: "They" are רבא and רב חסדא.

phrases.english: as it was stated:
If he thought it was an animal and it turned out to be a person,
phrases.notes: The killer in this case is a גר תושב who thought killing this victim was allowed.

phrases.english: or a non-Jew and it turned out to be a גר תושב.
Rava says: He is liable,
since one who says it is permitted is close to intentional.
Rav Chisda says: He is exempt,
since one who says it is permitted is forced by circumstances.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the exchange in steps 9 to 13 to a broader dispute between רבא and רב חסדא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא holds that אומר מותר is close to מזיד and is liable. רב חסדא holds that אומר מותר is an אנוס and is exempt. Each one's answer to the contradiction fits his own view.
steps.whatToRemember: The core dispute: אומר מותר is קרוב למזיד (רבא) or אנוס (רב חסדא). This is why each sage answered the contradiction differently.

steps.title: רבא challenges רב חסדא from the death decree on אבימלך
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the פסוק where God tells אבימלך he will die for taking שרה. He suggests this means a human court would execute him, even though he thought it was permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב חסדא: 'You shall die for the woman you took.' Doesn't this mean death by a human court?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב חסדא's view that an אומר מותר is exempt, using the story of אבימלך. אבימלך took שרה thinking she was not married, yet God told him he would die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבימלך is a classic אומר מותר: אברהם had said שרה was his sister. If he still deserved death בידי אדם, then an אומר מותר is liable. That would support רבא and go against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: By human hands, meaning a punishment carried out by a court
'Is it not...?', a way of suggesting how a source should be read

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Chisda:
"You shall die for the woman you took."
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:3. God is speaking to אבימלך about שרה.

phrases.english: Is it not that he deserved death by the hands of man?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 14 showed that רבא and רב חסדא disagree about אומר מותר. Here רבא brings a פסוק against רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that an אומר מותר is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אבימלך thought שרה was available, yet he was sentenced to death. If that death is בידי אדם, an אומר מותר is liable.

steps.title: The death was by Heaven, not by a court
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that אבימלך's death sentence was בידי שמים. The wording 'from sinning against Me' supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means death at the hands of Heaven. The wording also shows this, since it says 'from sinning against Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It says the death in the פסוק is a punishment from Heaven, not a court punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the death is only בידי שמים, the פסוק proves nothing about a human court. So רב חסדא can still say a court would not punish an אומר מותר. The words 'against Me' are read as hinting that this sin is between him and God only.

keyTerms.meaning: By the hands of Heaven, a punishment from God and not from a court
'It is also precise', meaning the exact wording supports this reading

phrases.english: No, it means at the hands of Heaven.
The wording is also precise, as it is written:
"from sinning against Me."
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:6. The point is the word 'Me': the sin is against God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in step 15 by reading the death as Heavenly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the death is בידי שמים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The death in the פסוק was a court execution, so an אומר מותר is liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The death was from Heaven, so the פסוק says nothing about court punishment.

steps.title: The proof from 'against Me' fails, as יוסף's פסוק shows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the wording. יוסף also called adultery a sin 'to God', yet adultery is punished by a court. So calling a sin 'against Me' does not rule out a human court, and here too אבימלך's judgment is given over to man.
steps.simpleTranslation: By your logic, when יוסף said 'and sin to God', would that mean to God and not to man? Rather, there his judgment is given to man, and here too his judgment is given to man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the support from 'from sinning against Me.' It shows that calling something a sin against God does not mean a court cannot punish it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף used similar words about adultery with the wife of פוטיפר, and that is certainly a court matter. So 'against Me' is no proof that אבימלך's punishment was only Heavenly. The גמרא concludes that here too his case belongs to a human court, so רבא's challenge against רב חסדא comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And according to your reasoning', which shows that the other side's logic leads to a wrong result
His judgment is given over to man, meaning a human court has the power to punish him

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not settle the law. It knocks down the defense of רב חסדא from step 16, so רבא's challenge from אבימלך stands again. Next, אביי attacks רבא from the same story.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
"and sin to God"
phrases.notes: בראשית 39:9. יוסף says this to the wife of פוטיפר.

phrases.english: would that mean to God and not to man?
Rather, his judgment is given over to man,
here too his judgment is given over to man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the support from the wording that step 16 brought.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both the proof from the wording ('from sinning against Me') and the answer that relied on it. The גמרא ends 'here too his judgment is given over to man,' which brings back רבא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A sin called 'against God' can still be punished by a human court, as יוסף's verse about adultery shows.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא from אבימלך's protest
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes אבימלך's protest, 'Will You slay even a righteous nation?' This suggests that an אומר מותר is innocent, which goes against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged רבא: 'Will You slay even a righteous nation?'
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבא is under attack. אביי uses אבימלך's own words, where he claims he is righteous because he did not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבימלך argues that acting without knowing the woman was married makes him a צדיק. If that claim is accepted, an אומר מותר is like an אנוס and should not be punished. That is רב חסדא's view, not רבא's.

keyTerms.meaning: A righteous nation, אבימלך's claim that he is innocent

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to Rava:
"Will You slay even a righteous nation?"
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:4. אבימלך says he is innocent because he did not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 17 restored רבא's challenge against רב חסדא. Now אביי attacks the other side, רבא, using the same אבימלך story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's view that an אומר מותר is close to a מזיד and is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אבימלך calls himself righteous because he did not know. This suggests that an אומר מותר is innocent.

steps.title: God's reply rejects אבימלך's claim of innocence
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that God's response, 'Return the man's wife, for he is a prophet', pushed back on אבימלך's claim. The explanation continues on the next daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is as they answered him: 'And now, return the man's wife, for he is a prophet.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to defend רבא. It points to God's reply, which shows that אבימלך's protest was not accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's proof works only if God agreed that אבימלך was righteous. The answer is that God's reply ('he is a prophet') was a rebuttal, not agreement. The full explanation of how this reply defeats his claim comes on the next daf.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that case or source
They responded to him, a reply that answers his claim

phrases.english: There, it is as they responded to him:
"And now, return the man's wife,
phrases.notes: בראשית 20:7

phrases.english: for he is a prophet"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering אביי's challenge from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the source in context: God's reply rejects the claim
steps.terutzHavaAmina: God accepted אבימלך's claim of innocence, so an אומר מותר is not liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: God answered and rejected the claim, so no proof can be taken from it. The explanation continues on the next daf.
